newsitem.title: USA: Boise Cascade in $650 million sale of mill, timber.
newsitem.headline: Boise Cascade in $650 million sale of mill, timber.

text.p: Boise Cascade Corp. said Monday it agreed to sell a pulp and paper mill in western Maine and 667,000 acres of supporting timberlands to Mead Corp. for $650 million.

Boise Cascade said the deal, expected to be finalized by year-end, would complete its departure from the coated paper business, allowing it to focus on uncoated free sheet paper, the standard for most home and office business machines.
Industry analysts said the deal would benefit both companies, reducing Boise Cascade's heavy debt burden and giving Mead potential economies of scale in the competitive market for coated paper.
In New York Stock Exchange trading, Boise Cascade was up $1.75 at $34.125, while Mead added 75 cents to $59.125.
"I think it's a strategic positive for both companies," said analyst Chip Dillon of Salomon Bros.
Boise Cascade said most proceeds from the sale of the Rumford, Maine, mill and nearby timberlands would be used to pay down the company's debt, which stood at $2.02 billion as of June 30.
Mead said the acquisition, which will nearly double the company's coated paper capacity to more than 1.25 million tons annually, will add to earnings next year.
Coated paper is used in books, magazines, catalogs and brochures and sells at a premium to most grades, although prices have been under pressure due to increased worldwide capacity.
"Coated paper is a targeted growth area for Mead -- we know this segment well, have invested heavily in it and have been successful," Mead Chairman Steven Mason said in a statement.
He said the new mill would offer "important synergies" with Dayton, Ohio-based Mead's existing facilities in Escanaba, Mich., and Chillicothe, Ohio.

Boise, Idaho-based Boise Cascade said it will continue to invest in boosting output of free sheet paper, including about $390 million in new equipment for its Jackson, Ala., facility, which is expected to begin adding to production in the spring.
The new equipment will raise uncoated free sheet capacity at the mill to 455,000 tons a year from 125,000.
Last year Boise Cascade produced a near-capacity 3.1 million tons of paper, including 1.2 million tons of uncoated free sheet and 443,000 tons of coated paper.
Much of the free-sheet paper went to its 80 percent-owned subsidiary Boise Cacade Office Products Corp.
Boise Cascade executives told analysts in a conference call that the sale would be "anti-dilutive" next year based on the debt reduction and improved efficiencies at its remaining plants.
Analyst Steven Dietrich of Jensen Securities estimated that sale could add 25 to 30 cents a share to Boise Cascade's annual earnings, which he estimated at $0.50 next year before the deal.
He estimated Boise Cascade would lose 50 cents a share this year after earning a record $5.39 a share last year.
